ITQAN:v4p311/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p311/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p311/r6.claim: The Qurʾān is an inimitable proof: the command to grant a polytheist protection until he hears God’s speech would not hinge on hearing it unless its hearing itself established the proof.
ITQAN:v4p311/r6.anchor: قال تعالى ﴿ وإن أحد من المشركين ﴾ استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r1.claim: The subject “any one” is raised by a verb explained by the following clause, since in governs a verb rather than a nominal subject.
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r1.anchor: {وإن أحد} رفع بفعل يفسره ما بعده لا بالابتداء لأن إن من عوامل الفعل.

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r2.claim: The polytheist here is one whom the Muslims had been ordered to fight.

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r3.claim: The polytheist seeks asylum after the sacred months have ended; the Prophet must grant protection rather than kill him hastily.
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r3.anchor:
{استجارك} أي : طلب منك الأمان والجوار بعد انسلاخ الأشهر الحرم.
{فأجره} فآمنه ولا تسارع إلى قتله.

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r4.claim: He is protected until he hears the Qur’an concerning obligations, reward, and punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r4.anchor:
{حتى يسمع} أي : إلى أن يسمع أو ليسمع.
{كلام الله} أي : القرآن فيما له وما عليه من الثواب والعقاب.

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r5.speaker: الأشعري
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r5.claim: Al-Ashʿari cites the verse to argue that one may hear God’s eternal speech, His attribute.
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r5.anchor:
استدل الأشعري بهذه الآية إلى أنه يجوز أن يسمع
388
الكلام القديم الذي هو صفة الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r6.speaker: الشيخ أبو منصور
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r6.claim: Abu Mansur rejects the claim that the eternal divine attribute itself can be heard.

BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r7.claim: The verse means hearing what signifies God’s speech, just as one hears news indicating someone’s knowledge; the attribute itself is not heard by the senses.
BURSEVI:v3p295#4/r7.anchor: فمعنى حتى يسمع كلام الله يسمع ما يدل عليه كما يقال سمعت علم فلان

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r1.claim: If the protected visitor does not convert after listening, escort him to his secure home among his people.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r1.anchor: {ثم أبلغه} بعد استماعه له إن لم يؤمن {مأمنه} أي : مسكنه الذي يأمن فيه

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r2.claim: The reason for granting asylum and safe escort is that the polytheists do not understand Islam; time to hear it removes their excuse.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r2.anchor:
{ذالك} يعني : الأمر بالإجارة وإبلاغ المأمن.
{بأنهم} أي : بسبب أنهم {قوم لا يعلمون}

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r3.claim: Jurists hold that a combatant who embraces Islam in enemy territory without learning ritual obligations owes no make-up after entering Muslim lands; one who converts within Muslim territory must make them up.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r3.anchor: حربي أسلم في دار الحرب ولا يعلم بالشرائع من الصوم والصلاة ونحوهما ثم دخل دار الإسلام

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r4.claim: Inwardly, the ego and its qualities do not know God’s kindness, turn instead to worldly desire, and are graciously given time to return to obedience.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r4.anchor: فكذا النفس وصفاتها قوم لا يعلمون الله وألطافه فلا يقبلون إليه ويعملون الدنيا وشهواتها

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r5.claim: An Israelite youth who worshipped twenty years and disobeyed twenty saw his gray hair, feared rejection, and heard God say that He had loved, left, and patiently awaited him, and would accept his return.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r5.anchor: أحببتنا فأحببناك وتركتنا فتركناك وعصيتنا فأمهلناك فإن رجعت إلينا قبلناك

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r6.claim: The servant should repent and seek forgiveness promptly; youthful repentance is weightier because desire is stronger, while old age weakens its call.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r6.anchor: وينبغي للعبد أن يسارع إلى التوبة والاستغفار فإن توبة الشاب أحسن من توبة الشيخ

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r7.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r7.claim: Saʿdi’s Persian verses mock repentance delayed until desire and worldly authority have faded, when resisting sin is easier.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r7.anchor: قحبه يراز نا بكارى ه كندتوبه نكند

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r8.claim: The Persian verse praises the young person able to sit in solitude as a lion in God’s way, despite difficulty rising from that corner.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r8.anchor:
جوان كوشه تشين شير مردراه خداست
كه يرخود نتواندز كوشة برخاست

BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r9.claim: The Arabic poem depicts an old man’s sins as too heavy for mounts, whitening his hair while darkening his heart.
BURSEVI:v3p295#5/r9.anchor:
شيخ كبير له ذنوب
تعجز عن حملها المطايا
قد بيضت شعره الليالي

QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r1.claim: A polytheist who asks protection must be sheltered until hearing God’s speech, then escorted to a place of safety if he does not believe.
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r1.anchor: إذا استجار المشرك - اليوم - فلا يرد حتى يسمع كلام الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r2.claim: If an unbeliever receives protection to hear God’s speech, a believer who seeks refuge from separation from God should not be barred from hearing Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r2.anchor: فإذا استجار المؤمن طول عمره من الفراق - متى يمنع من سماع كلام الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r3.claim: God’s protection of His friends from separation in the hereafter is a test of them, and the greatest terror will not grieve them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r3.anchor: كلا . . إنه يمتحنهم بذلك ، قال تعالى : { لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر }

QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r4.claim: If God shows care to those who lack knowledge, His care for those who know is greater; the spiritually bankrupt cannot equal the sincere, or the veiled equal those absorbed in divine presence.
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r4.anchor: فإذا كان هذا بره بمن لا يعلم فكيف بره بمن يعلم

QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r5.claim: A poem contrasts the faithful and deficient beloved, concluding that a lover and a hater are never equal.
QUSHAYRI:v1p408/r5.anchor: وأحبابنا شتان : واف وناقص . . . ولا يستوي قط محب وباغض

AKHFASH:v1p354/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p354/r1.claim: He prefers raising أحد with an understood verb as the more analogical parse, since conditional particles do not normally begin a clause with a noun.
AKHFASH:v1p354/r1.anchor: وقال {وأن أحد من المشركين استجارك} فابتدأ بعد (أن) ، وان يكون رفع أحدا على فعل مضمر أقيس الوجهين لأن حروف المجازاة لا يبتدأ بعدها.

AKHFASH:v1p354/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p354/r2.claim: Starting with a noun after أن is nevertheless attested because أن readily precedes nouns and no jussive verb follows overtly.
AKHFASH:v1p354/r2.anchor: الا انهم قد قالوا ذلك في "أن" لتمكنها وحسنها اذا وليتها الاسماء وليس بعدها فعل مجزوم في اللفظ

AKHFASH:v1p354/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p354/r3.claim: The line عاود هراءة وأن معمورها خربا is cited as an example of a noun following أن.

AKHFASH:v1p354/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r4.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p354/r4.claim: The line لا تجزعي أن منفسا أهلكته is another example of a noun following أن.
AKHFASH:v1p354/r4.anchor: لا تجزعي أن منفسا أهلكته * وأذا هلكت فعند ذلك فاجزعي

AKHFASH:v1p354/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r5.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p354/r5.claim: Some say أتجزع أن نفس أتاها حمامها is only recited with a raised noun because the verb is omitted and the noun is its cause.
AKHFASH:v1p354/r5.anchor: وقد زعموا أن قول الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الخامس والعشرون بعد المئتين] : أتجزع أن نفس أتاها حمامها * فهلا التي عن بين جنبيك تدفع

AKHFASH:v1p354/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p354/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p354/r6.claim: The verse can likewise be parsed with أحد raised by an understood verb.
AKHFASH:v1p354/r6.anchor: وهذا قد ابتدىء بعد "أن" وان شئت جعلته رفعا [127 ء] بفعل مضمر.

FARRA:v1p421/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p421/r1.claim: The protection command requires returning the polytheist to his place of safety.

FARRA:v1p421/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p421/r2.claim: The conditional verb remains jussive though أحد separates إن from it; إن uniquely permits such separation because it is a particle rather than a noun.
FARRA:v1p421/r2.anchor: في موضع جزم وإن فرق بين الجازم والمجزوم

FARRA:v1p421/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p421/r3.claim: Other intervening nominative or accusative words are likewise possible with إن; the cited verse and poetic line illustrate this looseness.
FARRA:v1p421/r3.anchor: وذلك سهل في (إن) خاصة دون حروف الجزاء

FARRA:v1p421/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r4.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v1p421/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows an accusative object before the jussive response but rejects a nominative subject in that position, since the response verb recalls its subject.
FARRA:v1p421/r4.anchor: وكان الكسائي يجيز تقدمة النصب في جواب الجزاء

FARRA:v1p421/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p421/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects al-Kisāʾī's exception: a conditional answer must take fa, or an equivalent jussive; without fa, a noun must contain the implied fa.
FARRA:v1p421/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك كما قال لأن الجزاء له جواب بالفاء

FARRA:v1p421/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p421/r6.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v1p421/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī cites a poem in which الخير appears accusative after a jussive conditional, but al-Farrāʾ parses it as an adjective of الأيام and reads تعقب as feminine.
FARRA:v1p421/r6.anchor: وكان الكسائي يجيز تقدمة النصب في جواب الجزاء

NAHHAS:v2p203/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p203/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p203/r4.claim: One who seeks protection is removed from the command to kill; أحد is nominative after an implied verb, acceptable with إن but awkward with other conditional particles.
NAHHAS:v2p203/r4.anchor: أي من القتل و ( أحد ) مرفوع بإضمار فعل كالذي بعده وهذا حسن في إن وقبيح في أخواتها

NAHHAS:v2p203/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p203/r5.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p203/r5.claim: Sibawayh explains the special treatment by calling إن the mother of conditional particles, since it is reserved for condition.
NAHHAS:v2p203/r5.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه في الفرق بين إن وأخواتها أنها لما كانت أم حروف الشرط

NAHHAS:v2p203/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p203/r6.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v2p203/r6.claim: Ibn Yazid rejects Sibawayh’s reason: إن can also mean ما, be extra, or be lightened from heavy inna, though it remains ambiguous.
NAHHAS:v2p203/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد أما قوله لأنها لا تكون في غيره فغلط لأنها تكون بمعنى ما

NAHHAS:v2p203/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p203/r7.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p203/r7.claim: Sibawayh cites an anonymous verse using إن منفسا أهلكته as evidence for conditional usage.
NAHHAS:v2p203/r7.anchor: وأنشد سيبويه ( لا تجزعي إن منفسا أهلكته … وإذا هلكت فعند ذلك فاجزعي

NAHHAS:v2p203/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p203/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p203/r8.claim: In ثم أبلغه مأمنه, the verb has two objects, one with its preposition omitted; مأمن has plural مآمن.
NAHHAS:v2p203/r8.anchor: ثم أبلغه مأمنه ) مفعولان حذف من أحدهما الحرف والجمع مآمن

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r1.claim: A polytheist who comes to hear the recitation and revelation is protected until he hears it.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد وان أحد من المشركين استجارك فاجره يقول : من جاءك واستمع ما تقول واستمع ما انزل اليك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r2.claim: Grant him safety until he hears God's speech.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله فاجره يقول : فهو امن حتى ياتيه فيسمع كلام الله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r3.speaker: السدي، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r3.claim: God's speech here is the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r3.anchor: عن السدى عن اصحابه في قول الله وان أحد من المشركين استجارك فاجره حتى يسمع كلام الله قال : كلام الله : القران وروى عن قتادة نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r4.claim: After hearing the message, escort him safely back where he came from.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ثم ابلغه مامنه من حيث جاء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r5.claim: A polytheist arriving without a treaty may be accepted or escorted to safety.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r5.anchor: قال عطاء في الرجل من اهل الشرك ياتي المسلمين بغير عهد قال : يخيره اما ان يقره واما ان يبلغه مامنه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r6.claim: If the visitor rejects the message, escort him to safety; Ibn Zayd says this ruling is not abrogated.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r6.anchor: ابن زيد في قوله ثم ابلغه مامنه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r7.claim: Those who do not know are those who do not reason.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1755/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس لا يعلمون يقول : لا يعقلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r1.claim: The asylum clause may elaborate the repentance condition or qualify the command to kill polytheists: spare one who seeks access to conduct an embassy or learn Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r1.anchor: لتفصيل مفهوم الشرط ، أو عطف على جملة { فاقتلوا المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r2.claim: The conditional formula emphasizes the rule and anticipates a request for protection; إن presents a hypothetical, rare condition so polytheists cannot claim they lacked a chance to meet the Prophet and use that as an excuse for continued idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r2.anchor: وجيء بحرف { إن } التي شأنها أن يكون شرطها نادر الوقوع للتنبيه على أن هذا شرط فرضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r3.claim: Al-Razi transmits that a polytheist asked Ali whether they would be killed if they came after the deadline to hear the Quran or for another need; Ali answered no and cited this verse, but Ibn Ashur says he could not locate the report and notes it would have occurred after revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r3.anchor: في ( تفسير الفخر ) أنه نقل عن ابن عباس قال : إن رجلا من المشركين قال لعلي بن أبي طالب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r4.claim: In a conditional, the indefinite one could mean the whole class or some individuals; explicitly saying one of the polytheists specifies universal coverage, and ahad derives from wahid and denotes an individual person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r4.anchor: وجيء بلفظ أحد من المشركين دون لفظ مشرك للتنصيص على عموم الجنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r5.claim: Putting one of the polytheists first focuses attention on the person seeking asylum before the request is mentioned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p117/r5.anchor: وتقديم { أحد } على { استجارك } للاهتمام بالمسند إليه ، ليكون أول ما يقرع السمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r1.claim: The indefinite noun may be initial because it is generic or because a conditional implies generality like a negation; a following verbal predicate licenses this order, and calling the noun an agent of an implied verb is only a grammatical interpretive device.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r1.anchor: ولذلك شاع عند النحاة أنه فاعل بفعل مقدر ، وإنما هو تقدير اعتبار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r2.claim: Universality and fronting emphasize protection for any polytheist with a sound reason to visit, even someone from a tribe that broke its pact, lest Muslims answer betrayal with betrayal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r2.anchor: تأكيد بذل الأمان لمن يسأله من المشركين إذا كان للقائه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ودخوله بلاد الإسلام مصلحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r3.claim: The Prophet's rule forbids betraying someone who betrayed you, supporting the prohibition on retaliatory treachery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r3.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ولا تخن من خانك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r4.claim: Seeking neighboring protection became a common metaphor for seeking security, since residence requires safety; ajara means secure, not make someone a neighbor, and the purpose is left to reasonable motives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r4.anchor: والاستجارة : طلب الجوار ، وهو الكون بالقرب ، وقد استعمل مجازا شائعا في الأمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r5.claim: Whether or not hearing the Quran was the visitor's original purpose, a temporary stay inevitably includes discussion and the Prophet's invitation to Islam; hearing God's speech marks the point when those purposes are complete.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p118/r5.anchor: جعل سماع هذا المستجير القرآن غاية لإقامته الوقتية عند الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r1.claim: God's speech means the Quran: God originated it to convey His intent and sent it through an angel to the Prophet, rather than a human composing it as with a hadith qudsi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r1.anchor: وكلام الله : القرآن ، أضيف إلى اسم الجلالة لأنه كلام أوجده الله ليدل على مراده من الناس وأبلغه إلى الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r2.claim: Thumma stresses the higher-priority duty to keep the visitor protected in Muslim territory until he reaches safety, even if that takes a long time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r2.anchor: للدلالة على وجوب استمرار إجارته في أرض الإسلام إلى أن يبلغ المكان الذي يأمن فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r3.claim: To deliver him to safety means let him go and do not harm him until he reaches safety; it does not require the Prophet to arrange an escort or transport.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r3.anchor: أمهله ولا تهجه حتى يبلغ مأمنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r4.claim: When a student asked permission to swallow his saliva, his teacher replied that he had granted him the Tigris and Euphrates, illustrating the idiom for asking someone to wait.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري : قلت لبعض أشياخي : ( أبلعني ريقي فقال قد أبلعتك الرافدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r5.claim: Ma'man means the visitor's own place of safety, normally his home territory, distinguished from temporary asylum by the possessive pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r5.anchor: مكان الأمن ، وهو المكان الذي يجد فيه المستجير أمنه السابق ، وذلك هو دار قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r6.claim: The final clause explains the whole command: protect the asylum seeker despite past harm until home because he does not know Quranic guidance; the wording both condemns his ignorance and explains the accommodation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p119/r6.anchor: فالإشارة إلى مضمون جملة : { فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.claim: After ordering combat, God commands that a polytheist seeking protection to hear the Qur’an and learn Islam be granted asylum, then safely escorted home if he does not accept the faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.anchor: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية بعد الأمر بقتال المشركين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the asylum rule is definitive and lasts until the Resurrection; Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi say it was abrogated by 9:5, while others limit it to the four-month period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: هي محكمة سنة إلى يوم القيامة، وقال مجاهد وقال الضحاك والسدي: هذا منسوخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.claim: Kalam Allah means the Qur’an, an adjective annexed to its described noun rather than a created thing annexed to its Creator; hearing means understanding its rulings, commands, and prohibitions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.anchor: وقوله سبحانه: حتى يسمع كلام الله يعني القرآن وهي إضافة صفة إلى موصوف لا إضافة خلق إلى خالق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.claim: Hearing is named because the ear leads to understanding; Arabic also uses hearing to mean comprehension, as when one says a listener did not hear a statement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.anchor: فذكر السماع بالأذان إذ هو الطريق إلى الفهم وقد يجيء السماع في كلام العرب مستعملا بمعنى الفهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.claim: Aḥad is raised by a verb explained by istajāraka; making it the subject is weak because the governing verb immediately follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.anchor: وأحد في هذه الآية مرتفع بفعل يفسره قوله استجارك ويضعف فيه الابتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.claim: Dhālika points to the kindness of asylum, hearing, and safe delivery; their lack of knowledge is failure to recognize guidance in following Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى هذا اللطف في الإجارة والإسماع وتبليغ المأمن ولا يعلمون نفي علمهم بمراشدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r1.claim: If a polytheist under a death order requests protection to hear the Qurʾan and consider its commands and prohibitions, grant refuge and then escort him to safety.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r1.anchor: استأمنك يبتغي أن يسمع القرآن وينظر فيما أمر به ونهي عنه فأجره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r2.claim: “They are a people who do not know” may explain why they are to be taught and protected: they lack knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r2.anchor: ذلك الذي أمرناك به من أن يعرفوا ويجاروا لجهلهم بالعلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase explains why a non-convert must be escorted back to safety: the people are ignorant of God’s command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p399/r3.anchor: من رده إلى مأمنه إذا امتنع من الإيمان لأنهم قوم جهلة بخطاب الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r1.claim: A polytheist seeking protection must be allowed to hear the Quran and a proof of the religion, then remain safe until escorted home; this lets the uninformed learn God's religion and lets His call spread.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r1.anchor: ليعلموا دين الله، وتنتشر دعوة الله في عباده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r2.claim: Any person who comes to hear what the Prophet says and what has been revealed is safe until hearing it and reaching the place from which he came.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r2.anchor: إنسان يأتيك يسمع ما تقول وما أنزل عليك، فهو آمن حتى يأتيك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r3.claim: The Prophet gave safe passage to Quraysh envoys at Ḥudaybiyyah, including ʿUrwa, Makraz, and Suhayl; impressed by Muslim reverence for him, they reported it at home and helped lead many to Islam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r3.anchor: فرأوا من إعظام المسلمين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما بهرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r4.claim: A messenger of Musaylimah affirmed his master's claim, so the Prophet said he would have beheaded him if envoys were killed; Ibn Masʿūd later executed him after he publicly endorsed Musaylimah outside a mission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r4.anchor: لولا أن الرسل لا تقتل لضربت عنقك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r5.claim: A visitor from enemy territory for a message, trade, peace, truce, tribute, or similar purpose receives protection until returning home; scholars disallow a full-year stay, permit four months, and differ on the interval between.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p113#2/r5.anchor: فطلب من الإمام أو نائبه أمانا، أعطي أمانا ما دام مترددا في دار الإسلام

JISHUMI:v4p3031/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r5.claim: Istijāra is seeking protection or a protector; granting protection makes the seeker safe, as if taking the person into one's neighborhood.
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r5.anchor: والاستجارة: طلب الجور أو المجير، والجار والمستجير بمعنى

JISHUMI:v4p3031/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r6.claim: بلاغ and إيصال both mean conveying to an endpoint; reaching a term may mean approaching its end rather than passing it.
JISHUMI:v4p3031/r6.anchor: والإبلاغ والإيصال من النظائر، والإبلاغ: التصيير إلى منتهى الحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r1.claim: God's “speech” may refer specifically to Sūrat al-Tawba, teaching the treaty and breach rulings and how to deal with polytheists differently from hypocrites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r1.anchor: أنه عني سورة براءة خاصة ليعلم ما فيها من حكم المقيم على العهد . وحكم الناقض له

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r2.claim: Alternatively, “speech of God” means the entire Qur'an, by which the seeker may be guided from error and return from unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r2.anchor: يعني القرآن كله , ليهتدي به من ضلاله ويرجع به عن كفره

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r3.claim: After the protection period expires, escort the seeker to safety if they remain in unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r3.anchor: يعني إن أقام على الشرك وانقضت مدة الأمان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r4.claim: Their lack of knowledge may mean failure to distinguish guidance from error or failure to know that their lives are exposed after their protection ends.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p341/r4.anchor: الرشد من الغي . والثاني : استباحة رقابهم عند انقضاء مدة أمانهم

MUJAHID:v1p273/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p273/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p273/r1.claim: A person among the polytheists may come to hear the message and revelation; he is safe until he hears God's speech and is then escorted to the place he came from.
MUJAHID:v1p273/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره ﴾ يقول إنسان يأتي فيسمع ما تقول ويسمع ما أنزل عليك فهو آمن

MUQATIL:9:6-10/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:6-10/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:6-10/r1.claim: If a Meccan polytheist seeks protection after fifty days, the Prophet must secure him from killing, let him hear the Quran, and return him safely if he refuses it; should he later fight and be captured, he may be killed.
MUQATIL:9:6-10/r1.anchor: فإن استأمنك أحد من المشركين بعد خمسين يوما فأمنه من القتل،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r1.claim: The conditional has an omitted verb governing أحد, understood as if it said: if someone from the polytheists seeks protection after the treaty months, grant it so he can hear monotheism and Qurʾān.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r1.anchor: أحد مرتفع بفعل شرط مضمر يفسره الظاهر أى وان استجارك أحد استجارك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r2.claim: He remains protected until he hears and reflects on God's word and understands the truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r2.anchor: ﴿ حتى يسمع كلام الله ﴾ ويتدبره ويطلع على حقيقة الامر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r3.claim: If he does not convert, escort him back to safety before fighting him if desired; a protected visitor must not be harmed or kept from returning, and may not settle in Muslim territory.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r3.anchor: ﴿ ثم أبلغه ﴾ بعد ذلك ﴿ مأمنه ﴾ داره التى يأمن فيها إن لم يسلم ثم قاتله إن شئت

NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r4.claim: The protection is given because they are ignorant of Islam and need security to hear and understand its truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p79/r4.anchor: بسبب أنهم قوم جهلة لا يعلمون ما الإسلام وما حقيقة ما تدعوا إليه فلا بد من اعطائهم الأمان

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r1.claim: A polytheist among those Muslims were ordered to fight who asks for protection should receive it so that he can hear and understand the Quran's rulings; if he accepts, well, otherwise he must be escorted to safety. Qurtubi says there is no disagreement on this.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r2.claim: If an enemy combatant encountered on a road in Muslim territory asks for protection, Malik considers the situation ambiguous and says to return him to safety.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r3.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qasim gives the same ruling for a trader who lands on the coast, believing traders could sell without being attacked: return him to safety.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r3.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: وكذلك الذي يوجد

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r4.claim: The verse's apparent case is protection for someone who wishes to hear the Quran and consider Islam; granting protection for other purposes is instead justified by Muslim interests.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r4.anchor: وظاهر الآية إنما هي فيمن يريد سماع القرآن والنظر في الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r5.claim: All scholars accept the ruler's grant of protection because he represents the public interest and acts for all in securing benefits and repelling harms.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r5.anchor: ولا خلاف بين كافة العلماء أن أمان السلطان جائز لأنه مقدم للنظر والمصلحة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r6.claim: All scholars accept a free man's protection pledge, though Ibn Habib says the imam should review it.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r6.anchor: فالحر يمضي أمانه عند كافة العلماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r7.claim: The well-known Maliki, Shafiʿi, Hanbali, and other juristic position permits a slave to give protection; Abu Hanifa and a second Maliki opinion reject it. Qurtubi prefers permission based on the hadith that even the lowest Muslim can guarantee protection, and says a free woman is still more entitled; lack of a war stipend is irrelevant.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r7.anchor: وأما العبد فله الأمان في مشهور المذهب وبه قال الشافعي وأصحابه وأحمد

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r8.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r8.claim: Ibn al-Majishun says a woman's protection is not effective unless the imam approves it, an isolated position against the majority.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: لا يجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r9.claim: A minor who is capable of fighting may give protection because he belongs to the fighting force and its defending unit.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r9.anchor: وأما الصبي فإذا أطاق القتال جاز أمانه لأنه من جملة المقاتلة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi hold that this verse was abrogated by the order to fight the polytheists.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r10.anchor: وقد ذهب الضحاك والسدي إلى أن هذه الآية منسوخة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r11.claim: Hasan and Mujahid say the verse remains operative until the end of time; Qurtubi endorses this as correct, citing ʿAli's refusal to kill a man seeking to hear God's word after the four-month period.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: هي محكمة سنة إلى يوم القيامة وقاله مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r12.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr recounts a polytheist asking ʿAli whether someone could visit Muhammad to hear God's word after the four-month grace period; ʿAli answers no one may kill him because this verse commands protection until he hears it.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r12.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: جاء رجل من المشركين

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r13.claim: Qurtubi rejects the claim that the protection rule applied only during the four-month truce and concludes that the verse is still operative.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6/r14.claim: In “in ahad,” “ahad” is nominative with an implied verb; this is acceptable after conditional “in” but improper with its sister particles, which Sibawayh distinguishes because “in” is specific to conditions.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid rejects Sibawayh's claim that “in” does not occur outside conditionals: it can mean “ma” or be a light form of emphatic “inna,” but remains ambiguous unlike the other particles.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد: أما قوله: «لأنها لا تكون في غيره» فغلط

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r2.claim: Sibawayh cites a line of poetry using conditional “in” to demonstrate its use in a conditional clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r2.anchor: وأنشد سيبويه: لا تجزعي إن منفسا أهلكته

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r3.claim: Scholars including Abu al-Hasan, al-Qadi Abu Bakr, al-Qalanisi, Ibn Mujahid, and al-Isfarayini infer that God's speech is heard when a reciter reads it, since the verse explicitly says “the speech of God” is heard.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r3.anchor: قاله الشيخ أبو الحسن والقاضي أبو بكر وأبو العباس القلانسي وابن مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r4.claim: Muslims say “we heard God's speech” when Quran is recited and distinguish it from recited poetry; Qurtubi recalls the doctrine that God's speech is neither letter nor sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:6#2/r4.anchor: إجماع المسلمين على أن القارىء إذا قرأ فاتحة الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that a polytheist asked ʿAlī whether he could approach the Messenger after the truce period to hear God's speech or seek another need; ʿAlī answered that he would not be killed, citing this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r1.anchor: نقل عن ابن عباس أنه قال : إن رجلا من المشركين قال لعلي بن أبي طالب إن أردنا أن نأتي الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r2.claim: Although expiration of the sacred months implies that proof had been established and excuses removed, a seeker of proof or the Qur'an must be granted safety, not killed, and escorted to safety.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r2.anchor: والمقصود منه بيان أن الكافر إذا جاء طالبا للحجة والدليل أو جاء طالبا لاستماع القرآن ، فإنه يجب إمهاله ويحرم قتله

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r3.claim: The rule shows that the purpose of fighting is acceptance of religion and monotheism and that inquiry into God's religion is among the highest ranks.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r3.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن المقصود من شرع القتل قبول الدين والإقرار بالتوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r4.claim: Grammatically, ahad is raised by an unspoken verb explained by istaǧāraka; it cannot be a subject because in does not govern nouns.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r4.anchor: أحد مرتفع بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر ، وتقديره : وإن استجارك أحد

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r5.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r5.claim: Sībawayh explains the unusual word order by fronting what matters most; here it emphasizes protecting a polytheist's blood despite the general order to fight.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r5.anchor: الحكمة فيه ما ذكره سيبويه ، وهو أنهم يقدمون الأهم والذي هم بشأنه

RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj paraphrases the rule as granting protection from killing until the person hears God's speech.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج : المعنى إن طلب منك أحد منهم أن تجيره من القتل إلى أن يسمع كلام الله فأجره

RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer from all kinds of people hearing God's speech that it consists of audible letters and sounds, and because ordered sounds arise successively, it is created.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r1.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : هذه الآية تدل على أن كلام الله يسمعه الكافر والمؤمن والزنديق والصديق

RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r2.speaker: الحشوية والحمقى
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r2.claim: The Hashwiyya and other foolish people combine the claims that God's speech is only letters and sounds and that those letters and sounds are eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r2.anchor: وأما الحشوية والحمقى من الناس ، فقالوا ثبت بهذه الآية أن كلام الله ليس إلا هذه الحروف والأصوات

RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن فورك
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r3.claim: Abū Bakr Ibn Fūrak says that hearing the letters and sounds also means hearing God's eternal speech; the other Ashʿarī scholars reject his claim.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r3.anchor: زعم أنا إذا سمعنا هذه الحروف والأصوات فقد سمعنا مع ذلك كلام الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r4.claim: The author rejects both identifying eternal speech with audible letters and claiming that those sounds let us hear a separate, distinct entity, since no such separate thing is heard.
RAZI-FULL:v15p181#2/r4.anchor: والأول : هو قول الرعاع والحشوية وذلك لا يليق بالعقلاء . وأما الثاني : فباطل

RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r1.claim: The Ashʿarī answer is that the sounds heard now are human acts, distinct from the original sounds God created; the same objection therefore applies to the Muʿtazilites.
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r1.anchor: هذا الذي نسمعه ليس عين كلام الله على مذهبكم ، لأن كلام الله ليس إلا الحروف والأصوات التي خلقها أولا

RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r2.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī proposed that God's speech is a distinct entity persisting with every reader, but the Muʿtazilites all rejected this unusual position.
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r2.anchor: واعلم أن أبا علي الجبائي لقوة هذا الإلزام ارتكب مذهبا عجيبا فقال : كلام الله شيء مغاير للحروف والأصوات وهو باق

RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r3.claim: The verse shows religious imitation alone is insufficient: a seeker is given time and safety to examine proof, so faith requires inquiry and argument.
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r3.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن التقليد غير كاف في الدين وأنه لا بد من النظر والاستدلال

RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r4.claim: The length of the safe-conduct period is not specified and depends on custom; continue it while the person shows signs of seeking truth, but not when he is merely delaying with lies.
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r4.anchor: ليس في الآية ما يدل على أن مقدار هذه المهلة كم يكون ولعله لا يعرف مقداره إلا بالعرف

RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r5.claim: The protection extends by analogy to anyone seeking evidence or answers to doubts, because the stated rationale is that the seeker does not know and pursues guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v15p182/r5.anchor: ويلتحق به كونه طالبا لسماع الدلائل ، وكونه طالبا للجواب عن الشبهات

SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r1.claim: إن أحد has the same الاشتغال construction as إن امرؤ in 4:176 according to the majority of grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r1.anchor: في كونه من باب الاشتغال/ عند الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r2.claim: حتى may mark an endpoint or a reason and on either reading attaches to فأجره.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r2.anchor: حتى " يجوز أن تكون هنا للغاية، وأن تكون للتعليل، وعلى كلا التقديرين يتعلق بقوله: " فأجره

SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r3.claim: The majority reject making حتى govern both استجارك and فأجره because the second verb would require an omitted pronoun in the genitive, which حتى only permits under poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r3.anchor: لا يجوز عند الجمهور لأمر لفظي من جهة الصناعة لا معنوي، فإنا لو جعلناه من التنازع

SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r4.claim: Grammarians who allow حتى to govern a hidden pronoun can permit the تنازع, with the second verb deleting its object as in فرحت ومررت بزيد.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6/r4.anchor: وأما عند من يجيز أن تجر المضمر فلا يمتنع ذلك عنده، ويكون من إعمال الثاني لحذفه

SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r1.claim: كلام الله is an adjective-to-described-noun possessive construction, not a created-object-to-Creator construction.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r1.anchor: كلام الله } من باب إضافة الصفة لموصوفها لا من باب إضافة المخلوق للخالق

SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r2.claim: مأمنه can mean the place of his safety or his reaching safety, as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:9:6#2/r2.anchor: و " مأمنه " يجوز أن يكون مكانا أي مكان أمنه، وأن يكون مصدرا أي: ثم أبلغه أمنه

STUDYQURAN:9:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r1.claim: An idolater seeking asylum is to hear the Quran and Islamic teachings, then be escorted safely until reaching home.
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r1.anchor: idolaters could come and hear the Quran and the teachings of Islam and then be taken to a place of safety

STUDYQURAN:9:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r2.claim: Commentators disagree whether 9:6 was abrogated by verses such as 47:4, which allows freeing prisoners or holding them for ransom; the dominant view says neither verse was abrogated.
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r2.anchor: The dominant opinion, however, is that neither 9:6 nor 47:4 was abrogated

STUDYQURAN:9:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r3.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r3.claim: On the dominant view, from the start of the war years, beginning at Badr, the Prophet and believers could kill the enemy, take prisoners, or release them.
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r3.anchor: the Prophet and the believers were given the authority to slay the enemy, take them prisoner, or release them from the very beginning of the years of war

STUDYQURAN:9:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r4.claim: Commentators differ over how much Quran an asylum seeker must hear: some require all of it, while others limit it to this sūrah's essential message for idolaters.
STUDYQURAN:9:6/r4.anchor: some saying it should be the entire Quran, others restricting it to this sūrah, since it contains the essence of what idolaters need to hear

TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r1.claim: A polytheist seeking protection to hear the Qur’an must be granted safety, have God’s speech recited to him, and be escorted back if he declines Islam; he is ignorant of faith’s proof and stakes.
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r1.anchor: وهو القرآن الذي أنزله الله عليه {فأجره} [التوبة: 6] يقول: فأمنه {حتى يسمع كلام الله} [التوبة: 6] وتتلوه عليه.

TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that the seeker is one of the polytheists whom the Prophet had been ordered to fight.
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك} [التوبة: 6] أي من هؤلاء الذين أمرتك بقتالهم {فأجره} [التوبة: 6] "

TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies God’s speech here as the Qur’an.
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي: " {فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله} [التوبة: 6] أما كلام الله: فالقرآن "

TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the person remains safe while listening and until returned to the place from which he came.
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: " {وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره} [التوبة: 6] قال: إنسان يأتيك

TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r5.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r5.claim: Saʿid recounts an enemy combatant asking to hear God’s speech; the Muslims ask him to testify and disavow idols, and he says he has done so.
TAB-FULL:v11p346#2/r5.anchor: عن سعيد، قال: " خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غازيا، فلقي العدو، وأخرج المسلمون رجلا من المشركين وأشرعوا فيه الأسنة، فقال الرجل

TAB-FULL:v11p348/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says that if the listener does not accept the message, he is to be escorted safely away; he denies that the rule is abrogated.

TAB-FULL:v11p348/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak is reported to regard the command to kill polytheists in 9:5 as superseded by the permission to release or ransom captives in 47:4.
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك: " {فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم} [التوبة: 5] نسختها: {فإما منا بعد وإما فداء} [محمد: 4] "

TAB-FULL:v11p348/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r3.claim: Qatada reports the reverse abrogation direction: the command in 9:5 supersedes the command to take captives and bind them in 47:4.
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " {حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق} [محمد: 4] نسخها قوله:

TAB-FULL:v11p348/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r4.claim: Al-Tabari rejects abrogation: no proof establishes an earlier universal duty to kill every polytheist that a later permission to pardon or ransom could cancel.
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي قول من قال: ليس ذلك بمنسوخ،

TAB-FULL:v11p348/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r5.claim: Killing, release without payment, and ransom were all part of the Prophet’s practice from Badr; the command thus leaves these options available rather than requiring killing in every case.
TAB-FULL:v11p348/r5.anchor: فكان الفداء والمن والقتل لم يزل من حكم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم من أول حرب حاربهم، وذلك من يوم بدر،

TABATABAI:9:1-16#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#2/r7.claim: The asylum command lets a polytheist seeking protection hear God's speech and then be escorted to safety; although it interrupts the withdrawal of protection, it answers a necessary concern because the mission seeks to guide people from shirk to monotheism.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#2/r7.anchor: الآية تتضمن حكم الإجارة لمن استجار من المشركين لأن يسمع كلام الله

TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r1.claim: The duty to spare a treatyless polytheist remains whenever there is hope that hearing the truth will guide him; killing is warranted only after hope ends.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r1.anchor: ولازم ذلك الإعتناء التام بكل طريق يرجى فيه الوصول إلى هداية ضال والفوز بإحياء حق

TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r2.claim: If a polytheist seeks protection to examine the true call, the believer must secure him until he hears God’s word, then return him safely so he can choose freely.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r2.anchor: فإذا استجار المشرك لينظر فيما تندب إليه الدعوة الحقة ويتبعها إن اتضحت له كان من الواجب إجارته حتى يسمع كلام الله

TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r3.claim: Once he persists in error after the proof, his protection ends and he may be killed by whatever means is easiest.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r3.anchor: فإذا تمادى بعد ذلك في ضلاله وأصر في استكباره صار ممن ارتفع عنه الأمان

TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r4.claim: This verse qualifies the preceding general command to kill polytheists wherever found.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r4.anchor: وقد بان بما قدمناه أولا أن الآية مخصصة لعموم

TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r5.claim: Hearing God’s word sets the limit of the asylum: after the seeker can distinguish guidance from error, he must be returned to his own safe place.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#3/r5.anchor: { حتى يسمع كلام الله } غاية للاستجارة والاجارة

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r1.claim: God’s word means the Qur’an generally, with relevant passages chosen to explain divine knowledge, religion, and the seeker’s doubts; restricting it to monotheism, Bara’a, or its opening seasonal verses lacks evidence.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r1.anchor: وبذلك يظهر فساد ما قيل إن المراد بكلام الله آيات التوحيد من القرآن

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r2.claim: Hearing means understanding religion’s foundations; for a non-Arab who cannot understand Arabic, the goal is comprehension rather than listening to Arabic recitation itself.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r2.anchor: أن المراد بسمع كلام الله الوقوف على أصول الدين ومعالمه

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r3.claim: The ruling is decisive and remains un-abrogated: accountability and severity come only after the proof is made clear.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r3.anchor: فالآية محكمة غير قابلة للنسخ إلى يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r4.claim: The claim that 9:6 was abrogated by the command to fight all polytheists is false; 9:6 remains binding until the end of time.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر فساد قول من قال أن قوله

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r5.claim: The verse protects someone seeking asylum for a religious purpose that may benefit his faith; it does not establish a general right of refuge for unrelated reasons.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r5.anchor: الآية إنما توجب إجارة المستجير إذا استجار لأمر ديني

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r6.claim: The instruction to escort the seeker safely preserves freedom in his life and choices, leaving people accountable on clear evidence after the messengers.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r6.anchor: التحفظ على حرية الناس في حياتهم وأعمالهم الحيوية

TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r7.claim: The verse also supports that belief in religion’s foundations must rest on certain knowledge, not even strong probability.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#4/r7.anchor: الاعتقاد بأصل الدين أن يكون عن علم يقيني لا يداخله شك

TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r1.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r1.claim: The Qummi commentary says to recite and explain the message to the seeker, then leave him alone until he returns to his safe place.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r1.anchor: إقرأ عليه وعرفه ثم لا تتعرض له حتى يرجع إلى مأمنه

TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r2.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r2.claim: When asked whether someone could still meet the Prophet after the four months without protection, Ali answered yes and cited the instruction to grant asylum to any polytheist who seeks it.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#22/r2.anchor: يا ابن أبي طالب فمن أراد منا أن يلقى رسول الله في بعض الأمر من بعد انقضاء الأربعة فليس له عهد قال علي بلى

TABATABAI:9:1-16#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#28/r2.claim: A polytheist who seeks protection must be sheltered until hearing God’s speech, then escorted to safety, because the people do not know.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#28/r2.anchor: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه

TABATABAI:9:1-16#30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:1-16#30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:1-16#30/r4.claim: God ends the polytheists’ pact for their breach but grants a reprieve, honors those who keep their pact, and requires notice before ending a pact for feared betrayal.
TABATABAI:9:1-16#30/r4.anchor: وكذا يأمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إن خاف من قوم خيانة أن ينقض عهدهم

TABRISI:9:5-6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:5-6/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:5-6/r5.claim: In “if anyone of the polytheists seeks your protection,” a hidden verb raises “one”; it means “if anyone seeks refuge with you.” Al-Zajjāj rejects raising it as a subject because a conditional clause’s governing verb cannot skip it.
TABRISI:9:5-6/r5.anchor: وقوله: { أحد } فإعرابه أنه مرفوع بفعل مضمر الذي ظهر تفسيره

TABRISI:9:5-6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:5-6/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:9:5-6/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī counters that a jussive verb may follow a conditional subject; the usual conditional answer has an underlying verb, and Sībawayh permits the construction criticized by al-Zajjāj.
TABRISI:9:5-6/r6.anchor: ولكن لا يمتنع أن يقع الجزم بعد الفاعل في الجزاء كما يقع في الشرط

TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r3.claim: A polytheist may seek protection after the four months to hear the Qurʾān and its proofs; grant safety and time to understand it, then escort him to his secure homeland if he does not convert, lest protection become betrayal.
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r3.anchor: معناه وإن طلب أحد من المشركين الذين أمرتك بقتالهم منك الأمان من القتل

TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r4.claim: The verse says “God’s speech” because the Qurʾān contains the main body of the proofs; those people are ignorant of faith and its evidence, so they should hear and consider it. This rebuts the claim that religious knowledge is innate and necessary.
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r4.anchor: وإنما خص كلام الله لأن معظم الأدلة فيه

TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r5.claim: The recited and heard Qurʾān is itself God’s speech: ordinary Arabic and legal convention call an author’s words “the speech” or “poetry” of that author, despite recitation.
TABRISI:9:5-6#3/r5.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن المتلو والمسموع كلام الله لأن الشرع والعرب جعلا الحكاية كعين المحكي

THALABI:v5p13/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p13/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p13/r1.claim: إن أحد من المشركين استجارك means ‘if one of the polytheists seeks your protection’; the wording is explained through Arabic usage and poetry.
THALABI:v5p13/r1.anchor: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك معناه وإن استجارك أحد

THALABI:v5p13/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p13/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p13/r2.claim: The Prophet must shelter a hostile polytheist after the sacred months so he can hear God’s word and learn the proof and religion; if he converts he joins the Muslims, and if not he must be escorted safely home.
THALABI:v5p13/r2.anchor: فأجره فأعذه وأمنه حتى يسمع كلام الله فتقيم عليه حجة الله

THALABI:v5p13/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p13/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p13/r3.claim: If the escorted person later fights and is captured, he may be killed; the reason given is that the polytheists do not know God’s religion and unity.
THALABI:v5p13/r3.anchor: فإن قاتلك بعد ذلك فقدرت عليه فاقتله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون دين الله وتوحيده

THALABI:v5p13/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p13/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v5p13/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the asylum command remains in force until the Day of Resurrection and has not been abrogated.
THALABI:v5p13/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: وهذه الآية محكمة إلى يوم القيامة وليست بمنسوخة

THALABI:v5p13/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p13/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v5p13/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says a polytheist asked Ali whether someone could come to Muhammad after the truce to hear him or meet a need; Ali answered yes and cited this verse.
THALABI:v5p13/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: جاء رجل من المشركين إلى علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n10/r1.claim: Seeking protection literally means seeking to become someone’s neighbour, invoking an ancient Arabian duty to protect and honour neighbours that Islam strongly affirms.
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n10/r1.anchor: a metaphorical expression denoting a demand for protection, based on the ancient Arabian custom

ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r1.claim: Razi glosses “his place of security” as the seeker’s homeland.
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r1.anchor: "his place of security" (ma'manahu)- i.e., "let him rejoin his homeland" (Razi)

ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r2.claim: Sending the protected person home leaves him free to accept or refuse the Qur’anic message and reaffirms that faith cannot be coerced.
ASAD-NOTES:9:6#n11/r2.anchor: he is free to accept or not to accept the message of the Qur'an

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298/r1.claim: In the conditional, istajāraka is jussive though ahad separates it from in; such separation is tolerated especially with in, which is a conditional particle rather than a noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298/r1.anchor: {استجارك} في موضع جزم وإن فرق بين الجازم والمجزوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r1.claim: The seeker of protection is a polytheist who had no treaty.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r2.claim: He is one of the polytheists whom the Prophet had been ordered to fight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r3.claim: A man asked ʿAlī whether a polytheist arriving after the truce to hear God’s word or meet a need would be killed; ʿAlī cited this verse and said no.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r3.anchor: جاء رجل من المشركين إلى علي بن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r4.claim: The request is for protection from killing while the person hears God’s word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r4.anchor: إن طلب منك أحد منهم أن تجيره من القتل إلى أن يسمع كلام الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r6.claim: “God’s word” includes promises of reward and punishment and the religious obligations of prayer, alms, fasting, pilgrimage, and other duties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p298#3/r6.anchor: لأوليائه من الثواب ولأعدائه من العقاب وما افترض في دينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r1.claim: Bring the person to a place where he is safe; the explanation assumes he has not converted, while a convert becomes a brother in religion.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r2.claim: If the recitation does not persuade the seeker, escort him to safety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r2.anchor: يقول: إن لم يوافقه ما تتلو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r3.claim: They need protection and instruction because they are ignorant of God’s religion, unity, and obligations, and may recognize Islam when taught.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r3.anchor: وجب أن يعرفوا ويجاروا؛ لجهلهم بالعلم فربما يتبينون به الإسلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r4.claim: Give refuge until the seeker hears God’s word, establish the proof and explain the religion; if he converts he enters Islam’s protection, and if not, return him safely without harassment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r4.anchor: فإن أسلم فقد دخل في عز الإسلام وإن أبى فأبلغه مأمنه ولا تعرض له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r5.speaker: أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r5.claim: A belligerent normally enters Muslim territory with his wealth as war booty unless seeking protection for instruction or trade; a child’s or insane person’s pledge is an ambiguous safe-conduct, while messengers and visitors retrieving protected property also receive safe passage home with person and property protected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p299/r5.anchor: الكافر الحربي إذا دخل دار الإسلام كان مغنوما مع ماله إلا أن يدخل مستجيرا لغرض شرعي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r3.claim: If an enemy asks for protection, grant it so he can hear the Quran and receive God’s proof; then escort him to safety, even if he remains in shirk, so he can decide what to do.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r3.anchor: فاجعله في أمن { حتى يسمع كلام الله } القرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:5-6/r4.claim: They are ignorant people who do not know God’s religion and oneness.

ELMALILI:9:6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r1.claim: Seeking protection means asking the Prophet for safe conduct and shelter from attack after the announced period has ended.
ELMALILI:9:6/r1.anchor: mühlet-i mezkûre çıktıktan sonra sana istîmân eder, senin kendisine eman verip câr olmanı

ELMALILI:9:6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r2.claim: The protection lets the seeker hear the Qur'an and proofs of truth, reflect, and learn the truth of the invited religion; for a speaker of Arabic, hearing may suffice for understanding.
ELMALILI:9:6/r2.anchor: Kur’ân’ı ve delâil-i Hakk’ı işitsin, düşünsün, senin davet ettiğin dinin hakikat ve hakkiyetine muttali‘olmak imkânını elde etsin

ELMALILI:9:6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r3.claim: A report says a polytheist asked Ali whether anyone seeking Muhammad after the deadline to hear God's word or for another need would be killed; Ali answered no and cited this verse.
ELMALILI:9:6/r3.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Hazret-i Ali’ye müşriklerden bir adam geldi, “bu mühletin inkizâsından sonra şayet bizden bir kimse kelâmullâhı dinlemek için veya diğer bir hâcet için Muhammed’e gelecek olursa katlolunacak mı?” dedi

ELMALILI:9:6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r4.claim: Some interpreters resolve the apparent conflict with Ali's report by restricting the other need to religious matters, since asking questions and hearing proofs also counts as hearing God's word.
ELMALILI:9:6/r4.anchor: Bunun için denilmiştir ki hâcetten murad herhangi bir hâcet-i dünyeviye değil, dine müte‘allik hâcettir

ELMALILI:9:6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r5.claim: The author sees no conflict and does not restrict the request to religious needs: the protection request is unrestricted, while listening to God's word describes the grantor's purpose.
ELMALILI:9:6/r5.anchor: Fakat dikkat olunursa muhalefet yoktur, hâceti böyle tahsise lüzum da yoktur. Zira âyette isticâre mutlaktır

ELMALILI:9:6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r6.claim: Safe conduct is obligatory when the seeker requests it for a religious purpose, but not obligatory for an unrestricted or worldly purpose; circumstances may make granting or refusing it appropriate or obligatory.
ELMALILI:9:6/r6.anchor: istîmân ederse eman vermek vâcib olur

ELMALILI:9:6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r7.claim: If an unbeliever seeks proofs of divine unity and prophethood to believe on evidence, Muslims must present the proofs; a belligerent may not be killed before that case is made.
ELMALILI:9:6/r7.anchor: Bir kâfir, an delîlin itikad etmek için bizden tevhid ve risaletin delâilini beyan ve ikāme-i hüccet talebinde bulunursa tevhîd-i ilâhîyi ve Hazret-i Peygamber’in sıhhat-i nübüvvetini beyan ile ikāme-i hüccet üzerimize vâcib olur

ELMALILI:9:6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r8.claim: The duty to teach also follows when anyone asks for an explanation of a matter relevant to their affairs.
ELMALILI:9:6/r8.anchor: her kim bizden umûruna müte‘allik bir şeyin târifini talep ve iltimas ederse tâlimi üzerimize vâcib olur

ELMALILI:9:6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r9.claim: Jurists hold that a belligerent entering Islamic territory under protection for a lawful religious purpose or trade is protected, even when the guarantee came from a minor or an insane person.
ELMALILI:9:6/r9.anchor: Fukaha demişlerdir ki: Bir harbî dâr-ı İslâm’a dâhil oluverirse kendisi ve malı ganimet olur

ELMALILI:9:6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r10.claim: Jurists treat a diplomatic mission as safe conduct, and protection for a person's property as also protecting them when they enter to retrieve it.
ELMALILI:9:6/r10.anchor: Herhangi birisi dâr-ı İslâm’a bir elçilikle giderse elçilik emandır. Birisi dâr-ı İslâm’daki bir malını almak için gider ve o malın da emânı bulunursa malın emânı onun da emânı olur

ELMALILI:9:6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r11.claim: After the visitor has heard the message, escort an unbelieving non-convert safely back to their secure place; a protected visitor may not be detained longer than needed.
ELMALILI:9:6/r11.anchor: istimâ‘ettikten sonra iman etmezse canı ve malı taarruzdan masûn olarak onu eman yeri olan mahalline, vatanına yetiştir. Binâen‘aleyh müste’menin fazla bir müddet durdurulması da câiz değildir

ELMALILI:9:6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:6/r12.claim: They are called people who do not know because they lack knowledge of faith and its rulings; protection allows them to hear the truth and removes their excuse.
ELMALILI:9:6/r12.anchor: İman ve İslâm’ın hakikat ve ahkâmını bilmezler ve hatta bu Arab müşrikleri her hususta câhil bir kavimdirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r45.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r45.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r45.claim: Even amid this firm policy, verse 6 immediately preserves the Prophet’s mercy by requiring protection for a polytheist who seeks it, even after the grace period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r45.anchor: Resûlullah’ın herkes için rahmet olduğu gerçeği ve İslâm’ın hoşgörü anlayışı böyle kesin tavır almayı gerektiren bir durumda dahi hemen dikkat çekmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r46.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r46.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r46.claim: Protection lets an uninformed polytheist learn and consider Islam, preventing verse 5 from being misread as coercion that would foster merely outward, hypocritical conversion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r46.anchor: böyle bir güvence sağlanmasının amacı, yeterli bilgi sahibi olmayan putperestlerden isteyenlere Allah’ın dinini daha yakından tanıma ve üzerinde düşünme fırsatı vermektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r47.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r47.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r47.claim: The guarantee must remove pressure and fear: the seeker is only to hear God’s message, and if he declines, he must be released and escorted to safety; thereafter he knowingly chooses either to leave the sacred zone or enter conflict, while the restriction on killing is geographically limited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r47.anchor: Şayet bu imkân sağlandıktan sonra o kişi kendi tercihiyle baş başa kalmak istiyorsa sadece serbest bırakılmakla yetinilmeyecek, güvende olacağı yere kadar ulaştırılacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r48.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r48.speaker: İslâm âlimleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r48.claim: Scholars infer a duty to explain monotheism and Muhammad’s prophethood to any non-Muslim who asks, even from an enemy community, and to honor guarantees for protected entrants whether they come to learn, trade, visit, or conduct diplomacy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r48.anchor: İslâm âlimleri bu âyetten, müslümanların, –kendilerine savaş açtıkları bir topluluğun üyesi bile olsa– Allah’ın birliği ve Hz. Muhammed’in peygamberliği konusunda delil gösterilmesini isteyen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r49.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r49.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r49.claim: Some exegetes use the phrase “hearing God’s word” to discuss the nature of divine speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:1/r49.anchor: Âyetteki “Allah’ın kelâmını işitme” anlamına gelen ifadeden hareketle bazı müfessirler Allah’ın sözünün mahiyeti konusundaki tartışmalara yer verirler

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r1.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say the safe-conduct verse was abrogated by the command to kill polytheists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك والسدي: هي منسوخة بآية الأمر بقتل المشركين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say the verse remains in force until the Day of Judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: هي محكمة إلى يوم القيامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr recounts that Ali said a person seeking to hear God's word or ask for help after the deadline must not be killed, citing this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r3.anchor: وعن ابن جبير: جاء رجل إلى علي رضي الله عنه فقال: إن أراد الرجل منا أن يأتي محمدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r4.claim: Although one view limits the rule to the four-month respite, Abu Hayyan's apparent position is that it remains binding; it qualifies the preceding commands to kill, capture, and besiege when a person seeks guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r4.anchor: وقيل: هذه الآية إنما كان حكمها مدة الأربعة الأشهر التي ضربت لهم أجلا، والظاهر أنها محكمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r5.claim: A polytheist asking for safe conduct to examine Islam must be protected until he hears and reflects on God's word, then escorted to a safe home if he does not convert; he may later be fought without treachery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r5.anchor: فالمعنى: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك، أي طلب منك أن تكون مجيرا له وذلك بعد انسلاخ الأشهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r6.claim: حتى can mark an endpoint or purpose and in either analysis attaches to فأجره; it cannot be treated as syntactic competition with استجارك because the majority say حتى cannot govern a pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r6.anchor: وحتى يصح أن تكون للغاية أي: إلى أن يسمع. ويصح أن تكون للتعليل، وهي متعلقة في الحالين بأجره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r7.claim: The Qur'an is the greatest miracle, so hearing it is named as the path to understanding; كلام الله is an attribute annexed to its describer, not a created object annexed to its Creator, and مأمنه means place of safety or safety itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r7.anchor: ولما كان القرآن أعظم المعجزات، علق السماع به، وذكر السماع لأنه الطريق إلى الفهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r8.claim: The Mu'tazilites infer that God's speech is created because what can be heard is letters and sounds, which are necessarily originated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p374/r8.anchor: وقد استدلت المعتزلة بقوله: «حتى يسمع كلام الله» على حدوث كلام الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r1.claim: The verse makes inquiry into divine unity a high religious station, since even a person otherwise liable to death is protected to investigate and must be escorted to safety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r1.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن النظر في التوحيد أعلى المقامات، إذ عصم دم الكافر المهدر الدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r2.claim: The verse shows that mere imitation is insufficient and that the seeker must be protected while hearing; after the hearing period a non-Muslim cannot simply remain in Muslim territory and must be returned home.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r2.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أنه بعد سماع كلام الله لا يقر بأرض الإسلام، بل يبلغ مأمنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r3.speaker: الأوزاعي، والثوري، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق، ومحمد بن الحسن، وأبو ثور، وداود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r3.claim: These authorities, and the well-known Maliki position, allow a free man to grant safe conduct; Abu Hanifa and one Maliki view deny it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r3.anchor: قال الأوزاعي، والثوري، والشافعي، وأحمد، وإسحاق، ومحمد بن الحسن، وأبو ثور، وداود: له الأمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r4.claim: The majority allow a free woman to grant safe conduct, and a boy capable of fighting may also grant it; Ibn Habib leaves the slave's status to the Imam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r4.anchor: والحرة لها الأمان على قول الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r5.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r5.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun says a free woman may grant protection only with the Imam's approval; Abu Hayyan calls this an anomalous opinion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: لا، إلا أن يجيره الإمام، وقوله شاذ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that they do not know Islam or the truth of the message, so they must be protected until they hear and understand it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r6.anchor: قاله الزمخشري. وقال ابن عطية: إشارة إلى هذا اللطف في الإجارة والإسماع وتبليغ المأمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p375/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the phrase refers to the gentleness of granting protection, letting them listen, and escorting them home; they lack knowledge of the right path in following the Messenger.
